newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.11 pct in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.11 pct in volatile trade.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.11 percent to close at 1.0682 per dollar in volatile trade Tuesday on the commercial foreign exchange market due to a low supply of dollars, dealers said.
Despite strong dollar inflows last week, the market does not have many dollars because the banks sold dollars to the Central Bank through an auction on Friday, dealers added.
The local currency traded between 1.0674 and 1.0685, following the direction of dollar flows.
At 1630 local/1930 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $24 million surplus Tuesday.
The market is expecting a new decline in the reais-dollar mini-band in coming days. The current mini-band was set by the Central Bank on Friday at between 1.0660 and 1.0710.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0710, up 0.01 percent.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.26 percent to end at 1.130, according to traders.
